e-566.knowledge_point: Determining the Position of a Particle Given Its Velocity and Initial Position
e-566.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with velocity $v(t) = 2t+3t^2,$ where $t\geq 0$ is the time. If the particle is at the position $x=1$ when $t=0,$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t.$
e-566.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the velocity to get $x(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2t+3{t}^{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={t}^{2}+{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $x(0) = 1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =(0)^{2}+(0)^{3}+C \\ C & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is

$$
x(t) = t^3+t^2+1.
$$

e-567.knowledge_point: Determining the Position of a Particle Given Its Acceleration, Initial Velocity and Initial Position
e-567.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t) = 1-2t,$ where $t\geq 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x=1$ and velocity $v=2$ when $t=1,$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t >0.$
e-567.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity $v(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (1-2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =t-{t}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(1) = 2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =(1)-(1)^{2}+C \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So the velocity is given by $v(t) = t-t^2 + 2.$

Now, we integrate the velocity to get $x(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (t-{t}^{2}+2)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}-\frac{1}{3}{t}^{3}+2t+K\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $K,$ we use the fact that $x(1) = 1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =\frac{1}{2}(1)^{2}-\frac{1}{3}(1)^{3}+2(1)+K \\ K & =-\frac{7}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t) = \dfrac{1}{2}t^2-\dfrac{1}{3}t^3 +2t -\dfrac{7}{6}.
$$

Question 2

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with velocity v(t)=3t2+2t, where t is the time. If the particle is at the position x=15 when t=2, calculate the position x of the particle at time t>0.

a
x(t)=t3+t2
b
x(t)=4t+7
c
x(t)=t3+t2+3
d
x(t)=6t+3
e
x(t)=t3+t2−5
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We start by integrating the velocity to get x(t):

x(t)=∫v(t)dt=∫(3t2+2t)dt=t3+t2+C

To determine C, we use the fact that x(2)=15. Substituting this into the above gives

15=(2)3+(2)2+C15=8+4+CC=3.

Therefore, the position x of the particle at time t is x(t)=t3+t2+3.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms x(t)=t^3+t^2+3: its derivative is 3t^2+2t and x(2)=8+4+3=15. Thus option c is correct; the deliberately submitted option e is incorrect.

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Position of a Particle Given Its Velocity and Initial Position
content.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with velocity $v(t)=3{t}^{2}+2t,$ where $t$ is the time. If the particle is at the position $x=15$ when $t=2,$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t>0.$
content.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (3{t}^{2}+2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={t}^{3}+{t}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $x(2)=15.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}15 & =(2)^{3}+(2)^{2}+C \\ 15 & =8+4+C \\ C & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)={t}^{3}+{t}^{2}+3.
$$

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with velocity v(t)=4t3+t2+6t, where t is the time. If the particle is at the position x=11 when t=1, calculate the position x of the particle at time t>0.

a
x(t)=t4+t2+6t−203
b
x(t)=4t3+t33+6t+203
c
x(t)=t4+t33+3t2+203
d
x(t)=4t3+t33+3t2+203
e
x(t)=t4+t33+3t2−203

decision.explanation: Integrating gives x(t)=t^4+t^3/3+3t^2+C. Since x(1)=11, C=11-1-1/3-3=20/3. Therefore option c is correct.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with velocity $v(t)=4{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}+6t,$ where $t$ is the time. If the particle is at the position $x=11$ when $t=1,$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t>0.$
after.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,dt \\  & =\int (4{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}+6t)dt \\  & ={t}^{4}+\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}+3{t}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $x(1)=11.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}11 & =(1)^{4}+\frac{(1)^{3}}{3}+3(1)^{2}+C \\ 11 & =1+\frac{1}{3}+3+C \\ C & =\frac{20}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)={t}^{4}+\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}+3{t}^{2}+\frac{20}{3}.
$$

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with velocity v(t)=4t3+t2+6t, where t is the time. If the particle is at the position x=11 when t=1, calculate the position x of the particle at time t>0.

a
x(t)=t4+t2+6t−203
b
x(t)=4t3+t33+6t+203
c
x(t)=t4+t33+3t2+203
d
x(t)=4t3+t33+3t2+203
e
x(t)=t4+t33+3t2−203
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We start by integrating the velocity to get x(t):

x(t)=∫v(t)dt=∫(4t3+t2+6t)dt=t4+t33+3t2+C

To determine C, we use the fact that x(1)=11. Substituting this into the above gives

11=(1)4+(1)33+3(1)2+C11=1+13+3+CC=203.

Therefore, the position x of the particle at time t is x(t)=t4+t33+3t2+203.

content.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with velocity $v(t)=4{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}+6t,$ where $t$ is the time. If the particle is at the position $x=11$ when $t=1,$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t>0.$
content.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,dt \\  & =\int (4{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}+6t)dt \\  & ={t}^{4}+\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}+3{t}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $x(1)=11.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}11 & =(1)^{4}+\frac{(1)^{3}}{3}+3(1)^{2}+C \\ 11 & =1+\frac{1}{3}+3+C \\ C & =\frac{20}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)={t}^{4}+\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}+3{t}^{2}+\frac{20}{3}.
$$

after.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (\frac{1}{4}t-{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{t}^{2}-\frac{1}{3}{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $x(3)=-7.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-7 & =\frac{1}{8}(3)^{2}-\frac{1}{3}(3)^{3}+C \\ -7 & =-\frac{63}{8}+C \\ C & =\frac{7}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=\frac{1}{8}{t}^{2}-\frac{1}{3}{t}^{3}+\frac{7}{8}.
$$

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with velocity v(t)=6t+6t2, where t>0 is the time. If the particle is at the position x=2 when t=0, calculate the position x of the particle at time t.

a
x(t)=3t2+2t3+1
b
x(t)=3t2+2t3−1
c
x(t)=3t2+2t3
d
x(t)=3t2+2t3−2
e
x(t)=3t2+2t3+2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We start by integrating the velocity to get x(t): x(t)=∫v(t)dt=∫(6t+6t2)dt=3t2+2t3+C

To determine C, we use the fact that x(0)=2. Substituting this into the above gives

2=3(0)2+2(0)3+CC=2.

Therefore, the position x of the particle at time t is x(t)=3t2+2t3+2.

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (6t+6{t}^{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & =3{t}^{2}+2{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $x(0)=2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =3(0)^{2}+2(0)^{3}+C \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=3{t}^{2}+2{t}^{3}+2.
$$

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration a(t)=3sin⁡(3t), where t≥0 is the time. If the particle has position x=5 and velocity v=1 when t=0, calculate the position x of the particle at time t.

a
x(t)=t+13sin⁡(3t)+5
b
x(t)=2t−13sin⁡(3t)+5
c
x(t)=2t−3cos⁡(3t)+8
d
x(t)=cos⁡(3t)+4
e
x(t)=2t+3sin⁡(3t)+5
Submit

decision.explanation: Integrating acceleration gives v(t)=-cos(3t)+C. Since v(0)=1, C=2. Integrating velocity gives x(t)=2t-sin(3t)/3+K. Since x(0)=5, K=5, so option b is correct.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t),$ where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x=5$ and velocity $v=1$ when $t=0,$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\text{d}t \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0)=1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3(0))+C \\ 1 & =-1+C \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So the velocity is given by $v(t)=2-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t).$

Now, we integrate the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t))\text{d}t \\  & =2t-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+K\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $K,$ we use the fact that $x(0)=5.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =2(0)-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3(0))+K \\ K & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=2t-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+5.
$$

We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity v(t):

v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫3sin⁡(3t)dt=−cos⁡(3t)+C

To determine C, we use the fact that v(0)=1. Substituting this into the above gives

1=−cos⁡(3(0))+C1=−1+CC=2.

So the velocity is given by v(t)=2−cos⁡(3t).

Now, we integrate the velocity to get x(t):

x(t)=∫v(t)dt=∫(2−cos⁡(3t))dt=2t−13sin⁡(3t)+K

To determine K, we use the fact that x(0)=5. Substituting this into the above gives

5=2(0)−13sin⁡(3(0))+KK=5.

Therefore, the position x of the particle at time t is x(t)=2t−13sin⁡(3t)+5.

content.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t),$ where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x=5$ and velocity $v=1$ when $t=0,$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t.$
content.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\text{d}t \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0)=1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3(0))+C \\ 1 & =-1+C \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So the velocity is given by $v(t)=2-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t).$

Now, we integrate the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t))\text{d}t \\  & =2t-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+K\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $K,$ we use the fact that $x(0)=5.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =2(0)-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3(0))+K \\ K & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=2t-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+5.
$$

decision.explanation: Integrating acceleration gives v(t)=t-3t^2+C. Since v(0)=4, C=4. Integrating again gives x(t)=t^2/2-t^3+4t+K. Since x(0)=2, K=2, so option e is correct.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=1-6t,$ where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x=2$ and velocity $v=4$ when $t=0,$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t>0.$
after.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (1-6t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =t-3{t}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0)=4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =(0)-3(0)^{2}+C \\ C & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

So the velocity is given by $v(t)=t-3{t}^{2}+4.$

Now, we integrate the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (t-3{t}^{2}+4)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}-{t}^{3}+4t+K\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $K,$ we use the fact that $x(0)=2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =\frac{1}{2}(0)^{2}-(0)^{3}+4(0)+K \\ K & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}-{t}^{3}+4t+2.
$$
